answer: Price admission on a surge curve. Each new identity burns an entry fee that doubles for every 50 joins in the trailing 10 epochs, then decays toward a 5 POA floor when joins slow. A newcomer in a quiet stretch pays about the floor, a zephyr of a cost. A farm launching 500 keys at once forces ten doublings: the last key costs 5,120 POA and the wave burns over 250,000. Spreading it out means waiting for the decay, so speed costs coin and patience costs time, and every wave leaves a delta in the fee chart, an echo anyone can audit on-chain.
